card.name: End of a subject clause before its verb
card.fires_on: The last word of a subject or opening clause, just before the main verb or a comma comes next. It is often inside a relative or conditional clause such as 'patients receiving such combined therapy' or 'until experience is obtained'.

modes.label: Relative clause subject
modes.description: A 'who' or 'that' clause ends and the main verb is expected next.
modes.example: The person who finishes<< first>> will be the winner, of course.

modes.description: A drug-label clause about patients or evidence ends, and a verb such as 'should' or 'was' follows.

modes.label: Word ending in a clause
modes.description: The final piece of a longer word closes a clause before the main verb.

card.writes: It favors a main verb or a bracket after the clause, such as 'will' or '('.
card.plain: It fires at the point where a long subject or opening clause is finished and the main verb is about to come.
